claim: The prompt-engineering sources define the practice as instruction design that leaves model parameters untouched.
quote: It involves strategically designing task-specific instructions, referred to as prompts, to guide model output without altering parameters.

claim: A catalog of prompt patterns frames prompts as a form of programming that can customize outputs and interactions.
quote: Prompts are also a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.

claim: The Prompt Report describes the field as suffering from conflicting terminology and a fragmented ontological understanding.
quote: it suffers from conflicting terminology and a fragmented ontological understanding of what constitutes an effective prompt due to its relatively recent emergence.

claim: A practitioner-based study calls prompt engineering a critical yet loosely defined skill.
quote: prompt engineering has emerged as a critical yet loosely defined skill.

claim: A survey of prompt and context engineering describes analyzing the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration.
quote: By analyzing the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration, we identify persistent limitations, such as context dilution and computational overhead.

claim: An oncology commentary argues that the future lies in better context, not just better prompts.
quote: emphasizing that the future of oncology AI lies in a better context, not just better prompts.

claim: The ACE framework defines context adaptation as modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence rather than weight updates.
quote: increasingly rely on context adaptation: modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence, rather than weight updates.

claim: A production-oriented survey lists context engineering alongside dynamic tool retrieval, execution methods, memory, and evaluation.
quote: a production-oriented framework covering dynamic tool retrieval, context engineering, execution methods, memory, and evaluation

claim: Empirical work attributes degradation to context itself, naming context rot as the progressive degradation of agent reasoning quality as the context window fills.
quote: a phenomenon now termed context rot has emerged: the progressive and nonlinear degradation of agent reasoning quality and tool calling reliability as the context window fills during extended coding sessions.

claim: One survey understands the agent harness as the external execution support structure built around the model.
quote: We understand the agent harness as the external execution support structure built around the model and treat it as a distinct performance lever that complements base model capability

claim: Another source names the memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification-and-governance layer as harness components.
quote: agent performance emerges from the interaction among the foundation model, memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification-and-governance layer.

claim: A modular harness for games composes perception, memory, and reasoning components.
quote: We introduce a modular harness design for LLM agents that composes of perception, memory, and reasoning components

claim: A harness for tool-integrated agents is described as scaffolding determining which tools are exposed and how they are described.
quote: the scaffolding that determines which tools are exposed, how they are described, and what auxiliary information accompanies each per-step observation.

claim: The externalization review presents harness engineering as the unification layer coordinating memory, skills, and protocols.
quote: harness engineering serves as the unification layer that coordinates them into governed execution.

claim: The same review traces a historical progression from weights to context to harness.
quote: We trace a historical progression from weights to context to harness

claim: The agent-loop survey takes the observe-decide-act loop as its unit of analysis.
quote: This survey takes that agent loop, not the model in isolation, as its unit of analysis

claim: HeavySkill describes agentic harnesses as orchestration frameworks coordinating multiple agents with memory, skills, and tool use.
quote: agentic harness with orchestration frameworks that coordinate multiple agents with memory, skills, and tool use

claim: Agentic RAG is described as going beyond the limits of traditional RAG by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline.
quote: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) transcends these limitations by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline.

claim: A harness-aware evaluation survey reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can reverse model rankings.
quote: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: UniACE reports that a benchmark score reflects a complete model–harness–environment configuration.
quote: a reported score reflects a complete model--harness--environment configuration rather than the model alone.

claim: One context-rot paper explicitly says no published study has tested its joint hypothesis.
quote: no published empirical study has directly tested the joint hypothesis that codebase scale drives context window growth
